title: Power-supply rejection ratio at DC (0.1 Hz small-signal), untrimmed core
claim: README.md 'Target specification (DRAFT)' row 'PSRR @ DC' (> 60 dB), for the 3.3 V primary flavor (DR-001). Records are PROVISIONAL against the draft spec until issue #1 ratifies it. Measures design/bandgap_core.sch open-circuit with a 1 V AC magnitude on the supply, so v(vref) is the supply-to-reference transfer function and PSRR = -db(v(vref)).

measurements.name: psrr_dc
measurements.note: Supply rejection at the lowest swept frequency (0.1 Hz), the DC figure the spec line asks for. Limit is the draft spec's > 60 dB target column; the > 70 dB stretch column is out of scope for wave 1 per DR-001's scope note.

measurements.name: f_dc
measurements.note: Index guard for psrr_dc: asserts that vector index 0 really is the 0.1 Hz point. Protects the DC rejection figure from being silently read off the wrong frequency if the sweep spec changes.

measurements.name: psrr_1k
measurements.note: Informational (no limit): rejection at 1 kHz. The spec line is DC only; this point is recorded so the roll-off is visible in the evidence trail and a later supply-noise question does not need a re-run.

measurements.name: f_1k
measurements.note: Index guard for psrr_1k: asserts that vector index 40 really is the 1 kHz point.

measurements.name: n_ac_points
measurements.note: Guard: asserts the AC sweep produced the expected 61 points (0.1 Hz .. 100 kHz, 10/decade). A collapsed sweep would make the indexed readouts above meaningless.

spread_checks.note: DC rejection must move by at least 0.5 dB across the 45-point matrix. A dead-flat result would mean the corner/temperature/supply knobs are not reaching the simulator.

notes: The AC magnitude of 1 V on the supply is a linearization scale factor, not a physical ripple amplitude: AC analysis is linear, so the transfer function is independent of it.

The large-signal DC counterpart of this quantity is measured independently by sim/line-regulation/ (its line_psrr_db measurement). The two should agree within a few dB; a large disagreement points at a bench error in one of them, which is why both are recorded.
